47703-wilford-woodruff-fourth-president-.creator: Unknown
47703-wilford-woodruff-fourth-president-.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. known to those familiar with Church history. Some of his life has been published in the _Deseret News,_ and _"Leaves from My Journal"_ contains important chapters. Magazines and Church publications have in them reminiscences which he has given to the readers of those periodicals at different times.

arxiv-2202-01835.title: Static solutions to the spherically symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system: a particle-number-Casimir approach
arxiv-2202-01835.creator: Håkan Andréasson
arxiv-2202-01835.description: Abstract Existence of spherically symmetric solutions to the Einstein-Vlasov system is well-known. However, it is an open problem whether or not static solutions arise as minimizers of a variational problem. Apart from being of interest in its own right, it is the connection to non-linear stability that gives this topic its importance.

arxiv-2202-12365.title: Alternative metrics to select motors for Quasi-Direct Drive actuators
arxiv-2202-12365.creator: Karthik Urs, Challen Enninful Adu, Elliott J. Rouse, Talia Y. Moore
arxiv-2202-12365.description: Abstract Robotic systems for legged locomotion—including legged robots, exoskeletons, and prosthetics—require actuators with low inertia and high output torque. Traditionally, motors have been selected for these applications by maximizing the motor gap radius. We present alternative metrics for motor selection that are invariant to transmission ratio.

arxiv-2206-01512.title: Latent Topology Induction for Understanding Contextualized Representations
arxiv-2206-01512.creator: Yao Fu, Mirella Lapata, mlap@inf.ed.ac.uk
arxiv-2206-01512.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yao Fu, Mirella Lapata, mlap@inf.ed.ac.uk. In this work, we study the representation space of contextualized embeddings and gain insight into the hidden topology of large language models. We show there exists a network of latent states that summarize linguistic properties of contextualized representations. Instead of seeking alignments to existing well-defined annotations, we infer this latent network in a fully unsupervised way using a structured variational autoencoder.

arxiv-2212-14566.title: Pontryagin Optimal Control via Neural Networks
arxiv-2212-14566.creator: Chengyang Gu, Hui Xiong, Yize Chen
arxiv-2212-14566.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Chengyang Gu, Hui Xiong, Yize Chen. Solving real-world optimal control problems are challenging tasks, as the complex, high-dimensional system dynamics are usually unrevealed to the decision maker. It is thus hard to find the optimal control actions numerically. To deal with such modeling and computation challenges, in this paper, we integrate Neural Networks with the Pontryagin’s Maximum Principle (PMP), and propose a sample efficient framework Neural-PMP. The resulting controller can be implemented for systems with unknown and complex dynamics.

arxiv-2303-08818.title: Boosting Convolutional Neural Networks’ Protein Binding Site Prediction Capacity using SE(3)-invariant transformers, transfer learning and homology-based augmentation
arxiv-2303-08818.creator: Daeseok Lee, Jeunghyun Byun, Bonggun Shin
arxiv-2303-08818.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Daeseok Lee, Jeunghyun Byun, Bonggun Shin. Figuring out small molecule binding sites in target proteins, in the resolution of either pocket or residue, is critical in many virtual and real drug-discovery scenarios. Since it is not always easy to find such binding sites based on domain knowledge or traditional methods, different deep learning methods that predict binding sites out of protein structures have been developed in recent years.

arxiv-2305-11982.title: Sequential Memory with Temporal Predictive Coding
arxiv-2305-11982.creator: Mufeng Tang, Helen Barron, Rafal Bogacz
arxiv-2305-11982.description: Abstract Forming accurate memory of sequential stimuli is a fundamental function of biological agents. However, the computational mechanism underlying sequential memory in the brain remains unclear. Inspired by neuroscience theories and recent successes in applying predictive coding (PC) to static memory tasks, in this work we propose a novel PC-based model for sequential memory, called temporal predictive coding (tPC).

arxiv-2311-09966.title: The divergence-free velocity formulation of the consistent Navier-Stokes Cahn-Hilliard model with non-matching densities, divergence-conforming discretization, and benchmarks Journal: Journal of Computational Physics
arxiv-2311-09966.creator: M.F.P. ten Eikelder, D. Schillinger
arxiv-2311-09966.description: Abstract The prototypical diffuse-interface model that describes multi-component flows is the Navier-Stokes Cahn-Hilliard model (NSCH). Over the last decades many NSCH models have appeared that claim to describe the same physical phenomena, yet are distinct from one another. In a recent article [M.F.P. ten Eikelder, K.G. van der Zee, I. Akkerman, and D. Schillinger, Math. Mod. Meth. Appl. S.

arxiv-2404-12707.title: Cosmology from String T-duality and zero-point length
arxiv-2404-12707.creator: G. G. Luciano, A. Sheykhi
arxiv-2404-12707.description: Abstract Inspired by String T-duality and taking into account the zero-point length correction, l 0 l_{0} , to the gravitational potential, we construct modified Friedmann equations by applying the first law of thermodynamics on the apparent horizon of the Friedmann-Robertson-Walker (FRW) Universe.

arxiv-2411-08009.title: Edge subdivisions and the L 2 L^{2} -homology of right-angled Coxeter groups
arxiv-2411-08009.creator: Grigori Avramidi, Boris Okun, Kevin Schreve
arxiv-2411-08009.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Grigori Avramidi, Boris Okun, Kevin Schreve. If L L is a flag triangulation of S n − 1 S^{n-1} , then the Davis complex Σ L \Sigma_{L} for the associated right-angled Coxeter group W L W_{L} is a contractible n n -manifold. A special case of a conjecture of Singer predicts that the L 2 L^{2} -homology of such Σ L \Sigma_{L} vanishes outside the middle dimension. We give conditions which guarantee this vanishing is preserved under edge subdivision of L L .

arxiv-2503-22492.title: Reaching Classicality through Transitive Closure
arxiv-2503-22492.creator: Quentin Blomet a,b and Bruno Da Ré c,d
arxiv-2503-22492.description: Abstract Recently, Da Ré et al. ((2023)) showed that all logics based on Boolean Normal monotonic three-valued schemes coincide with classical logic when defined using a strict-tolerant standard ( 𝐬𝐭 \mathbf{st} ). Conversely, they proved that under a tolerant-strict standard ( 𝐭𝐬 \mathbf{ts} ), the resulting logics are all empty.

arxiv-2504-20637.title: Protocol Dialects as Formal Patterns: A Composable Theory of Lingos Technical report
arxiv-2504-20637.creator: Víctor García, Santiago Escobar, Catherine Meadows, Jose Meseguer
arxiv-2504-20637.description: Abstract Protocol dialects are methods for modifying protocols that provide light-weight security, especially against easy attacks that can lead to more serious ones. A lingo is a dialect’s key security component by making attackers unable to “speak” the lingo. A lingo’s “talk” changes all the time, becoming a moving target for attackers.

arxiv-2509-24863.title: Vision At Night: Exploring Biologically Inspired Preprocessing For Improved Robustness Via Color And Contrast Transformations
arxiv-2509-24863.creator: Lorena Stracke, Lia Nimmermann, Shashank Agnihotri, Margret Keuper, Volker Blanz
arxiv-2509-24863.description: Abstract Inspired by the human visual system’s mechanisms for contrast enhancement and color-opponency, we explore biologically motivated input preprocessing for robust semantic segmentation. By applying Difference-of-Gaussians (DoG) filtering to RGB, grayscale, and opponent-color channels, we enhance local contrast without modifying model architecture or training.

arxiv-2510-08287.title: On the Cahn-Hilliard equation with nonlinear diffusion: the non-convex case
arxiv-2510-08287.creator: Monica Conti, Stefania Gatti, Andrea Giorgini & Giulio Schimperna
arxiv-2510-08287.description: Abstract . We investigate the Cahn-Hilliard equation with nonlinear diffusion and non-degenerate mobility modeling phase separation phenomena in complex systems (e.g., crystals and polymers). Previous results in the literature on this model relied on the strong convexity assumption of the gradient part of the energy, which excludes relevant cases.

arxiv-2511-10809.title: Near-optimal Linear Predictive Clustering in Non-separable Spaces via Mixed Integer Programming and Quadratic Pseudo-Boolean Reductions
arxiv-2511-10809.creator: Jiazhou Liang, Hassan Khurram, Scott Sanner
arxiv-2511-10809.description: Abstract Linear Predictive Clustering (LPC) partitions samples based on shared linear relationships between feature and target variables, with numerous applications including marketing, medicine, and education. Greedy optimization methods, commonly used for LPC, alternate between clustering and linear regression but lack global optimality. While effective for separable clusters, they struggle in non-separable settings where clusters overlap in feature space.

arxiv-2511-18302.title: The Catastrophic Paradox of Human Cognitive Frameworks in Large Language Model Evaluation: A Comprehensive Empirical Analysis of the CHC-LLM Incompatibility
arxiv-2511-18302.creator: Mohan Reddy
arxiv-2511-18302.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mohan Reddy. This comprehensive investigation presents an extensive empirical analysis of the fundamental incompatibility between human psychometric frameworks and Large Language Model (LLM) evaluation. Through systematic assessment of nine frontier models including GPT-5, Claude Opus 4.1, and Gemini 3 Pro Preview using the Cattell-Horn-Carroll (CHC) theory of intelligence, we reveal a catastrophic paradox that challenges the epistemological foundations of cross-substrate cognitive evaluation.

arxiv-2511-21377.title: Controlling changes to attention logits
arxiv-2511-21377.creator: Ben Anson, Laurence Aitchison
arxiv-2511-21377.description: Abstract Stability of neural network weights is critical when training transformer models. The query and key weights are particularly problematic, as they tend to grow large without any intervention. Applying normalization to queries and keys, known as ‘QK norm’, fixes stability issues in practice, but is not always applicable.

arxiv-2512-07781.title: Microquasar remnants as hidden PeVatrons Preprint: Leandro Abaroa
arxiv-2512-07781.creator: Leandro Abaroa, Gustavo E. Romero, Valentí Bosch-Ramon
arxiv-2512-07781.description: Abstract The Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO) has revealed numerous ultrahigh-energy gamma-ray sources of unknown origin. We propose that a fraction of them can be explained by microquasar remnants, i.e., binary systems where mass transfer has ceased and the central engine is quenched.

arxiv-2601-17637.title: Scaling Laws for Moral Machine Judgment in Large Language Models
arxiv-2601-17637.creator: Kazuhiro Takemoto
arxiv-2601-17637.description: Abstract Autonomous systems increasingly require moral judgment capabilities, yet whether these capabilities scale predictably with model size remains unexplored. We systematically evaluate 75 large language model configurations (0.27B–1000B parameters) using the Moral Machine framework, measuring alignment with human preferences in life-death dilemmas.

britannica-1911-poltergeist.title: Poltergeist (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-poltergeist.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-poltergeist.description: Article 'Poltergeist' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 22), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. applied to certain phenomena of an unexplained nature, such as movements of objects without any traceable cause, and noises equally untraced to their source; but in some cases exhibiting intelligence, as when raps answer a question by a code. In the word Poltergeist, the phenomena are attributed to the action of a Geist, or spirit: of old the popular explanation of all residuary phenomena.

Understanding the Sandia Message Rate
Benchmark

doe-osti-3818342-understanding-the-sandi.description: U.S. Department of Energy technical report. Modern HPC applications increasingly keep data resident in GPU memory, making host-only MPI measurements insufficient for

pmc-10622492.title: Provider and User Acceptability of Integrated Treatment for the Control of Malaria and Helminths in Saraya, South-Eastern Senegal
pmc-10622492.creator: Muhammed O. Afolabi, Aminata Diaw, El Hadji Babacar Fall, Fatimata Bintou Sall, Adams Diédhiou, Amadou Seck, Baba Camara, Diatou Niang, Isaac A. Manga, Ibrahima Mbaye, Ndèye Mareme Sougou, Doudou Sow, Brian Greenwood, Jean Louis A. Ndiaye
pmc-10622492.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). .Integration of vertical programs for the control of malaria, schistosomiasis, and soil-transmitted helminthiasis has been recommended to achieve elimination of malaria and neglected tropical diseases (NTD) by 2030. This qualitative study was conducted within the context of a randomized controlled trial to explore the perceptions and views of parents/caregivers of at-risk children and healthcare providers to determine their acceptability of the integrated malaria-helminth treatment approach.

pmc-10726828.title: The causal effects between selenium levels and the brain cortical structure: A two‐sample Mendelian randomization study
pmc-10726828.creator: Xiaowei Zhang, Yuqing Zhong, Kejun He
pmc-10726828.description: Extensive research has demonstrated the critical role of selenium (Se) and selenoproteins in brain function and cognition. However, the impact of Se on brain cortical structure remains enigmatic. Therefore, this study used Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis to investigate the causal effect between Se levels and brain cortical structure.

pmc-10735914.title: COGNITIVE TRAINING APPROACHES TO IMPROVE COGNITION AND ASSOCIATED FUNCTIONS IN MID TO LATE LIFE
pmc-10735914.creator: Ashley Curtis, Amy Costa, Madison Musich, Chloe Rzeppa, Christina McCrae
pmc-10735914.description: Cognitive Training (CT) has yielded inconsistent benefits in non-patient populations. Despite known cognition/sleep associations, limited studies have investigated CT’s impact on sleep. We examined cognitive and associated outcomes across three CT programs in older adult (OA) insomnia patients [with/without mild cognitive impairment (MCI)] and middle-aged adults (MA) with generalized anxiety disorder (GAD). In Study 1, OAs with insomnia (Mage=67.9±8.

pmc-10748378.title: Biochar Enhances the Resistance of Legumes and Soil Microbes to Extreme Short-Term Drought
pmc-10748378.creator: Kang He, Qiangbo Liu, Jialei Zhang, Guanchu Zhang, Guolin Li, Yousef Alhaj Hamoud, Hiba Shaghaleh, Tingting Chang
pmc-10748378.description: Short-term drought events occur more frequently and more intensively under global climate change. Biochar amendment has been documented to ameliorate the negative effects of water deficits on plant performance. Moreover, biochar can alter the soil microbial community, soil properties and soil metabolome, resulting in changes in soil functioning.

pmc-11600978.title: Association of depression with gastroesophageal reflux disease, and the mediating role of risk factors: a Mendelian randomization study
pmc-11600978.creator: Hui Duan, Lan Tao, Kaiwen Wu, Qian Li, Xinxu Zhou, Peiwen Dong, Xiaobin Sun, Lin Lin, Xiaolin Ma, Rong Zhao, Qiong Wang
pmc-11600978.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundGrowing evidence suggests that depression affects gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). But, the relationship between depression and GERD is unclear. To examine the relationship between depression and the risk of GERD, as well as the mediating role of risk factors.MethodsWe found genetic variants associated with GERD (N = 78,707) and depression (N = 500,199 (excluding 23 and Me) from the largest genome-wide association study and we applied two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) to find out if they are related.

pmc-11716750.title: Correlations of antemortem [18F]MK‐6240 PET with ROI‐matched postmortem biochemical assessment of total tau and tau phospho‐epitopes pThr181, pSer199, pThr231, and pSer396
pmc-11716750.creator: Tobey J. Betthauser, Eric E Abrahamson, Elena Ruiz De Chavez, Jordan P Teague, Andrew K McVea, Yuetiva Deming, Brooke E Schroeder, Madeleine R Barger, Sterling C. Johnson, Sanjay Asthana, Victor L Villemagne, Bradley T. Christian, Shahriar Salamat, Milos D Ikonomovic
pmc-11716750.description: Background[18F]MK‐6240 was developed for PET imaging of AD tau pathology, but the exact molecular signature of specific binding remains unclear. This study quantified levels of four phospho‐tau forms and total tau in postmortem brain tissues from [18F]MK‐6240 imaged cases to investigate associations with antemortem [18F]MK‐6240 PET.

pmc-12490220.title: Clinical and molecular dissection of CAR T cell resistance in pancreatic cancer
pmc-12490220.creator: M Angela Aznar, Charly R Good, Julie S Barber-Rotenberg, Sangya Agarwal, Wesley Wilson, Alex Watts, Zhen Zhang, Donna Gonzales, Greg Donahue, Wei-Ting Hwang, Austin K Rennels, Andrew J Rech, Shunichiro Kuramitsu, Hua Huang, Karl M Glastad, Katherine A Alexander, Gabriela Plesa, Emily Dowd, Andrea Br
pmc-12490220.description: SummaryPatients with advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) have a median survival of less than a year, highlighting the urgent need for treatment advancements. We report on a phase 1 clinical trial assessing the safety and feasibility of intravenous and local administration of anti-mesothelin CAR T cells in patients with advanced PDAC.

pmc-12821127.title: Prognostic nutritional index and 28-day mortality in elderly septic patients: A retrospective analysis based on the MIMIC database
pmc-12821127.creator: Yuewen Yang, Zhihong Zhou, Huajie Dai, Jian Zhong
pmc-12821127.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). OBJECTIVEPeripheral blood lymphocyte count and serum albumin level are crucial predictors of mortality across various diseases, including sepsis. However, previous studies have focused primarily on individual indicators (lymphocyte count or albumin) in relation to sepsis prognosis.

pmc-12916694.title: Endothelin-1 in the failing Fontan: pathobiology, precision therapeutics, and future trial design
pmc-12916694.creator: Iman Maiza
pmc-12916694.description: The Fontan circulation, devised as definitive palliation for single-ventricle congenital heart disease, imposes systemic venous hypertension, loss of pulmonary arterial pulsatility, and restricted preload reserve. These hemodynamic trade-offs progressively injure the pulmonary vasculature, liver, and lymphatic system, producing late morbidities including elevated pulmonary vascular resistance, Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD), protein-losing enteropathy, and arrhythmias.

pmc-13139267.title: Endovascular treatment of symptomatic vasospasm and delayed cerebral ischemia after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage – a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13139267.creator: Michael Veldeman, Tobias Rossmann, Roel Haeren, Hanna Schenck, Rahul Raj, Charlotte S. Weyland
pmc-13139267.description: BackgroundEndovascular rescue therapy, including intra-arterial spasmolysis and balloon angioplasty, is widely used for symptomatic vasospasm and delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI) after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH), but its impact on functional recovery is unclear. We systematically reviewed evidence on patient-centered outcomes, including effects by follow-up time, intervention type, and clinical severity.

pmc-13265076.title: Driver Drowsiness Detection using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques: A Systematic Review
pmc-13265076.creator: Saber Ghaffari fam, Ehsan Sarbazi, Senobar Naderian, Salman Khazaei, Mehmet Tatli, Hassan Soleimanpour
pmc-13265076.description: Introduction:Behavioral indicators have been increasingly utilized in machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) frameworks to enable automated driver drowsiness detection (DDD). This study aimed to investigate the available evidence on the modeling frameworks, datasets, input modalities, and performance metrics used in DDD systems.
